issue: Gloss mismatch: tangan = hand; 'arm' is lengan. Also 'boxes' plural is fine (unmarked), but the body-part gloss is wrong.

fix.target: Tangan saya sakit setelah mengangkat kotak berat.
fix.english: My hand hurts after lifting heavy boxes.

issue: Grammar tip is misleading: 'janji alone means promise' — janji alone also means appointment (the deck's own id-0609 tip says so: 'ada janji = have an appointment'). Internal contradiction.

fix.target: Saya mau membuat janji dengan dokter gigi.
fix.english: I want to make an appointment with the dentist.
fix.grammar: membuat janji = make an appointment: membuat janji dengan dokter gigi.

issue: Bare-root 'periksa' as main verb violates register policy rule 5 (cards model full meN- form; no tip notes the drop). Full form for having one's eyes checked is memeriksakan.

fix.target: Minggu lalu saya memeriksakan mata di klinik.
fix.english: Last week I had my eyes checked at a clinic.

issue: 'bisa menunggu besok' reads as 'can wait for tomorrow'; 'wait until tomorrow' needs sampai: menunggu sampai besok.

fix.target: Istirahat dulu, pekerjaan bisa menunggu sampai besok.
fix.english: Rest first, the work can wait until tomorrow.

issue: 'Angin bertiup kencang' is weather-report/news register, not conversational (policy rule 2: Q3 formality only where the situation is formal — casual weather talk is not). Speakers say 'anginnya kencang sekali'.

fix.target: Anginnya kencang sekali malam ini.
fix.english: The wind is really strong tonight.

issue: Time-word stacking: 'waktu malam hari' jams the conjunction waktu against the time noun phrase malam hari — clunky and non-idiomatic. Natural: 'kalau malam' or 'pada malam hari'.

fix.target: Kalau malam, suhu di sini turun.
fix.english: At night, the temperature here drops.

issue: 'siang tadi' is the marked order; idiomatic is 'tadi siang' (the deck itself uses 'tadi sore' in id-0523 and 'tadi siang' in id-0425). 'sangat panas' also stiffer than 'panas sekali' conversationally.

fix.target: Tadi siang cuaca di pantai panas sekali.
fix.english: At midday today the weather at the beach was very hot.

issue: Bare-root 'cek' as main verb; policy rule 5 says cards model the full meN- form (mengecek), tips may note the drop — no tip here.

fix.target: Saya selalu mengecek ramalan cuaca sebelum berangkat.
fix.english: I always check the weather forecast before leaving.

issue: Awkward noun-phrase stacking: 'Angin laut sore hari enak sekali di sini' strings angin laut + sore hari with no linker. Natural phrasing fronts the time: 'Kalau sore, angin lautnya enak.'

fix.target: Kalau sore, angin laut di sini enak sekali.
fix.english: In the late afternoon, the sea breeze here is really pleasant.

issue: 'kalau ombak besar' is clipped; the conditional wants the definite -nya: 'kalau ombaknya besar' (cf. 'jalanan licin' pattern the deck handles correctly in id-0532).

fix.target: Jangan berenang di laut kalau ombaknya besar.
fix.english: Don't swim in the sea when the waves are big.

issue: Grammar tip is factually wrong: it claims 'hujan + noun names the rain type' then gives 'hujan deras' as an example — deras is an adjective, not a noun. Sentence itself is fine.

fix.target: Kemarin hujan es turun di kota Bandung.
fix.english: Yesterday hail fell in the city of Bandung.
fix.grammar: hujan es = hail, literally 'ice rain': Kemarin hujan es turun.

issue: English-calque redundancy: 'Apa hobi kamu di waktu luang?' — a hobby is by definition what you do in free time; the tacked-on 'di waktu luang' mirrors awkward English, not Indonesian usage.

fix.target: Apa yang biasanya kamu lakukan di waktu luang?
fix.english: What do you usually do in your free time?
fix.grammar: waktu luang = free time: di waktu luang = in your free time.

issue: menyanyi is intransitive; with an object the verb is menyanyikan ('menyanyi lagu' is the colloquial drop the policy says not to model untagged). Standard: menyanyikan lagu.

fix.target: Anak saya suka menyanyikan lagu anak-anak.
fix.english: My child likes singing children's songs.
fix.grammar: menyanyikan = sing something: menyanyikan lagu = to sing a song.

issue: Gloss overshoots: 'sampai malam' = until night(fall); 'until late at night' is 'sampai larut malam' (larut already taught at id-0437).

fix.target: Kadang-kadang kami bermain kartu sampai larut malam.
fix.english: Sometimes we play cards until late at night.

issue: menari is intransitive; with a named dance as object the standard verb is menarikan (same transitivity issue as id-0570).

fix.target: Ibu saya suka menarikan tarian tradisional Bali.
fix.english: My mother likes dancing traditional Balinese dances.
fix.grammar: menarikan = dance a specific dance: menarikan tarian Bali.

issue: 'mengambil foto' is an English calque of 'take a photo'; the natural verb is memotret, which the deck itself uses at id-0600.

fix.target: Dia memotret pemandangan waktu jalan-jalan.
fix.english: He photographs scenery while traveling around.

issue: Register inconsistency in one sentence: bare-root 'saya dengarkan musik' (colloquial meN- drop, untagged — policy rule 5) alongside full-form 'membersihkan'. Model mendengarkan.

fix.target: Biasanya saya mendengarkan musik waktu membersihkan rumah.
fix.english: I usually listen to music while cleaning the house.

issue: Gloss error on a real-world trap: 'malam Jumat' means THURSDAY night (the eve of Friday, with spooky connotations to boot); 'Friday night' is 'Jumat malam'. Target and gloss contradict each other.

fix.target: Setiap Jumat malam kami berkumpul dan bernyanyi bersama.
fix.english: Every Friday night we get together and sing.
fix.grammar: Jumat malam = Friday night; malam Jumat means Thursday night (the eve of Friday).

issue: Gloss mismatch: masak = cook, but English says 'grill'; satay is grilled — the collocation is membakar sate (bakar sate). Also bare 'masak' reused untagged.

fix.target: Kadang-kadang kami membakar sate di halaman belakang.
fix.english: Sometimes we grill satay in the backyard.
fix.grammar: membakar = to grill or burn: membakar sate = to grill satay.

issue: Calque/ambiguity: 'tidak mendengar telepon kamu' reads as 'didn't hear your telephone (device)'. You hear the phone ring: tidak mendengar ponsel berbunyi, or telepon dari kamu for 'a call from you'.

fix.target: Maaf, tadi saya tidak mendengar ponsel saya berbunyi.
fix.english: Sorry, I did not hear my phone ring earlier.

newTokens.berbunyi: to ring, to make a sound
